sermon.title: God Reveals Himself to and Corrects Unbelievers Part 1
sermon.speaker: Pastor Kincer
sermon.summary: Daniel 4 shows God teaching a heathen king. In a dream a watcher ordered a great tree cut down, leaving a stump—Nebuchadnezzar—so that the living would know the Most High rules and sets up even the lowliest. Be a disciple, not just a believer.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear.

chunks.short_answer: A heathen king taught by God—Babylon corrected God’s people, then God revealed Himself to Babylon.
chunks.text:
In chapter 4, we’re going to see a heathen king being taught by God three important Bible truths. Three important, vital Bible principles. Okay? So, the title of this message, I got two titles again, is Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, is taught three important Bible truths by God himself. God comes and reveals himself to this man. The second title is God reveals himself to and corrects unbelievers, including government rulers, that God uses to correct God’s people.

See, Babylon was used to correct God’s people, but then God himself reveals himself to them and corrects them. That’s the nature of our God. So, Daniel chapter 4. The king in chapter 4 verses 1 through 5 has another troubling dream that made him afraid. Now, this time he understands the dream. He can describe it. And he’s terrified. He’s afraid. Daniel 1 verse 4. In Daniel 4, Nebuchadnezzar himself is writing this chapter. Okay? Probably taken from the king’s records. All right? But, this is Nebuchadnezzar himself talking.

This is not Daniel. I, Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, unto how many people? All people. Now, why is that phrase used? Because he wasn’t king of China, he wasn’t the king of Japan, he wasn’t the king of Australia or Americas. Because of the Revelation, God is speaking to all of us. Are you there? Okay, to all people, all languages, all nations. You hear this terminology used in the prophets and in the book of Revelation a lot. See, God is talking and when he talks to one person, he is using it to talk to all of us. Are you with me? All right. That dwell on all the earth. Peace be multiplied unto you. I thought it was good to show the signs and wonders that the high God has worked toward me.

Now, us Pentecostals, Charismatics, these faith camps and miracle camp, we’re really into signs and wonders, but one side, healings, changing water to wine, walking on water, you know, all these you know, highfalutin stuff. But here, in this book, is signs and wonders that us Pentecostals and Charismatics don’t like to talk about. Just remember that statement. All right. How great are his signs and how mighty are his wonders? This is a heathen king talking. Because God has revealed it to him. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom and his dominion is from generation to generation. Nebuchadnezzar didn’t even know God.

See, God revealed this to him way back before the New Testament was ever written. Now, in verses 6 through 7, the same advisors to the king. He’s still got these bombs around. They couldn’t do anything in chapter 2. They can’t [clears do anything now. Throat] The magicians, the astrologers, the Chaldeans, the soothsayers cannot make known the told dream. In chapter 2, the dream wasn’t told. They had to tell it and interpret it. Now they’ve been told it cuz they told the king in chapter 2, “Tell us the dream and we’ll interpret it.” But here in chapter 4, the king tells him the dream and they still can’t interpret it. And he still uses them for his advisers.

Nebuchadnezzar is a little slow like we are. You know, we’re a little slow. And I we we get in our little clicks and our little groups and we advise each other and we’re not getting anywhere and you know truth comes along and we’re a little slow to accept it, aren’t we? Yeah. So the dream is about a tree being cut down, leaving a stump, and I couldn’t find a stump with feathers and nails. No artist, no one understood that that the stump grew feathers, the stump grew nails, and the stump ate of the grass of the field. No one that I could find on the internet interpreted that. So I’m stuck with what they knew after Daniel told them. And I challenge you today, try and interpret this dream without Daniel and see what you come up with.

[clears. All right. Throat] So the king comes to Daniel and he says, “Daniel, in my dream I saw a strong tree, number one. One first part of the dream, a tree that grew to heaven in the midst of the earth seen to the end of all the earth. Now, we know that the empire of Babylon did not extend to the four corners of the earth. We know that by common sense, don’t we? But see, when God is talking through Revelation to all of us, he’s talking in a different sense. You got it? Cuz he’s wanting to speak to everyone in the earth. All right. [clears. Those leaves are beautiful, throat] there’s a lot of fruit in it, and it was food for all the animals that dwelled in its shadow, and all the birds that lived in its branches, and all flesh, all mankind was fed of it.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “The tree that you saw, which grew and became strong, whose height reached to the heavens and which could be seen by all the earth, whose leaves were lovely and its fruit abundant, in which was food for all, under which the beasts of the field dwelt, and in whose branches the birds of the heaven had their home— it is you, O king, who have grown and become strong; for your greatness has grown and reaches to the heavens, and your dominion to the end of the earth. “And inasmuch as the king saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven and saying, ‘Chop down the tree and destroy it, but leave its stump and roots in the earth, bound with a band of iron and bronze in the tender grass of the field; let it be wet with the dew of heaven, and let him graze with the beasts of the field, till seven times pass over him’; this is the interpretation, O king, and this is the decree of the Most High, which has come upon my lord the king: They shall drive you from men, your dwelling shall be with the beasts of the field, and they shall make you eat grass like oxen. They shall wet you with the dew of heaven, and seven times shall pass over you, till you know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever He chooses. “And inasmuch as they gave the command to leave the stump and roots of the tree, your kingdom shall be assured to you, after you come to know that Heaven rules.

faqs.question: When did God reveal this?
faqs.answer: Before the New Testament was written.

faqs.question: Who said cut it down?
faqs.answer: A watcher and a holy one.

faqs.question: What should you be?
faqs.answer: A disciple, not just a believer.
